films.title: V4.
films.description: BLAME's 16-minute Cleveland independent film brings together 26 skaters under Benny Liberatore's filming and editing. Premiered at The Happy Dog in Cleveland on December 26, 2025, the complete film arrived online in January 2026 alongside a first-party poster release.
creditNotes: BLAME's authorized complete-film description names all 26 featured skaters in appearance order and formally credits Benny Liberatore for filming and editing.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies V4. as a 16-minute 2026 BLAME independent film by Ben 'Benny' Liberatore, corroborates the complete 26-skater roster and records Cleveland as the location.
The official source does not publish a formal part hierarchy, so all 26 skaters remain under its featured-rider label rather than being assigned unsupported solo parts.
films.locationNote: The official description documents the Cleveland premiere, while SkateVideoSite independently identifies Cleveland as the film's location and BLAME as a Cleveland company.
films.historicalContext: V4. continues BLAME and Benny Liberatore's Cleveland video lineage after The Blame Video, Blame Style and V3, moving the series into a fourth installment with a 26-skater cross-section of the local and visiting scene.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1920x1080 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. The red BLAME identity frame is dedicated film artwork and the page carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: LCRMOV
films.description: Milan Stolper's 23-minute independent film crosses nine cities on three continents, centering seven starring riders and documenting 19 additional appearances. Stolper leads the production, with three named additional filmers and two further independently catalogued contributors.
creditNotes: Milan Stolper's authorized complete-film description distinguishes seven starring riders from 16 featured appearances and formally credits Vukman Milan, Igor Nowak and Kuba Gasior for additional filming.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies LCRMOV as a 23-minute 2026 film by Stolper, corroborates the starring and featured roster, and additionally catalogs Josh Dubski, Jay Figuora and Alex Decunha as appearances plus Wiktor Jakowski and Kacper Serkowski as production contributors.

The three archive-only appearances are retained in a separate group, while the two additional generic production contributors are not assigned narrower unsupported roles. Official spellings take precedence where the sources vary.
films.locationNote: The filmmaker's description names all nine cities, and SkateVideoSite independently records the same international footprint across the United States, Spain, United Kingdom, Thailand, Poland and Hungary.
films.historicalContext: Built over multiple years, LCRMOV is an unusually broad independent travel film spanning Gdansk, London, Los Angeles, Barcelona, Bangkok, San Francisco, Warsaw, Budapest and Krakow while preserving a clearly separated starring cast and international supporting roster.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. Its LCRMOV title treatment appears over a stylized city image and carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: Greyburn
films.description: Jeremy Przybyla's 18-minute Midwest film follows nine skaters through rough-edged street terrain across Wisconsin, Michigan and Indiana. Vague Skate Mag explicitly hosts the complete filmmaker-supplied film, with Przybyla credited for filming and editing and Harry Reynolds and Felix Meyers on additional cameras.

sharedSections: Nick Mistele / Sean Hanley / Benny Fosco

creditNotes: Vague Skate Mag's complete-film page and hosted player name all nine featured riders, formally credit Jeremy Przybyla for filming and editing, and identify Felix Meyers and Harry Reynolds for additional filming.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies Greyburn as an 18-minute 2026 independent film by Przybyla and corroborates the complete roster, camera credits, soundtrack section structure and Midwest context.
Shared sections are retained only where the independently catalogued soundtrack explicitly groups riders; no unsupported solo-part hierarchy is inferred.
films.locationNote: Vague's first-party hosting page explicitly says the film covers Wisconsin, Michigan and Indiana, while SkateVideoSite independently tags the film as a United States Midwest production.
films.historicalContext: Greyburn is a compact regional document of Midwest street skating that deliberately foregrounds weathered, irregular spots over polished plazas and connects crews across Wisconsin, Michigan and Indiana.
films.artworkNotes: The exact licensed upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. The image is a dedicated film still from the Greyburn page and carries no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.
